stem: A line of best fit for a set of data has a slope of \(-3\). The line predicts \(y = 42\) when \(x = 5\). What value of \(y\) does the line predict when \(x = 9\)?
solution: With slope \(-3\), \(y\) changes by \(-3 \times 4 = -12\), so the prediction is \(42 - 12 = 30\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This adds 12 instead of subtracting it; the slope is negative, so \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(42 - 3(9)\), which treats 42 as the \(y\)-intercept. The value 42 is the prediction at \(x = 5\), not at \(x = 0\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This subtracts 3 only once. The increase in \(x\) is 4, so \(y\) changes by \(-3 \times 4\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
f = -3 * (x - 5) + 42
r = f.subs(x, 9)
assert r == 30
assert value(choices[answer]) == r
assert all(value(choices[k]) != r for k in choices if k != answer)
